text:
sam: Heads-up — customer (ACME) is seeing intermittent 500s on /v1/generate and a few sporadic 401s. They gave an app trace but no request IDs. Can we ask for a tiny reproducible curl + SDK snippets and the exact request IDs/response headers?

maya: Yep. Ask them to run a single curl that forces an X-Request-ID and includes verbose output so we get headers + wire. Example to send them: 

```bash
# replace $API_KEY with their key
curl -i -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"open-7b","input":"hello"}' \
  --max-time 20 2>&1 | tee curl_verbose.txt
```

maya: Ask them to attach the produced curl_verbose.txt and highlight the full response headers (especially any X-Request-ID, X-Traceparent, X-RateLimit-*), and the HTTP status line. Also ask them to include the exact UTC timestamp they ran it.

sam: If they prefer SDKs, give these tiny snippets (no deps, single-file):

Python:
```python
import os, requests
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('API_KEY')}", "X-Request-ID": "rep-sample-123"}
resp = requests.post(url, json={"model":"open-7b","input":"hello"}, headers=headers, timeout=15)
print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.headers)
print(resp.text)
```

Node (fetch):
```js
// set process.env.API_KEY
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.API_KEY}`, 'X-Request-ID': 'rep-sample-123' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'open-7b', input: 'hello' })
  });
  console.log(res.status, Object.fromEntries(res.headers));
  console.log(await res.text());
})();
```

Go (net/http):
```go
package main
import ("bytes" "fmt" "net/http" "os")
func main(){
  body := bytes.NewBufferString(`{"model":"open-7b","input":"hello"}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST","https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", body)
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("API_KEY"))
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-ID","rep-sample-123")
  resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
  if err!=nil { fmt.Println("err:", err); return }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  fmt.Println("status:", resp.StatusCode)
}
```

ethan: Also request these extras from the customer: short bullet list —
- the raw response headers (not just body)
- the X-Request-ID value (if present) or the curl_verbose.txt
- client timezone and the exact UTC timestamp they saw the error
- application logs around that timestamp (30s before/after)
- whether they use a proxy, CDN, or API gateway that might mutate headers

julia: For the 401s specifically, ask them to run a single curl showing the Authorization header is present (you can instruct them to obfuscate the token) and to confirm if they rotate keys. Example: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" ...` and include the returned WWW-Authenticate header if any.

sam: If they can run a tiny capture locally, ask for both stdout and stderr from the curl/SDK run (we often get useful TLS/proxy errors there). If they can’t paste keys, they should still paste headers and the X-Request-ID.

maya: If they want, we can provide a one-line base64-able debug bundle command to collect app logs + environment snippet to speed triage. Example instructions to share with customer: 

1) Run the curl/python/js/go snippet above and save output.
2) Gather app logs (30s window).
3) Run: `tar czf debug_bundle.tgz curl_verbose.txt app.log && base64 debug_bundle.tgz > debug_bundle.b64`
4) Paste the debug_bundle.b64 file in a support reply (we’ll provide a secure upload if needed).

support-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-4587 — attach incoming debug bundle to this thread when available.

sam: Perfect. I'll post these snippets to the customer now and ask them to run the commands and attach the files. Once they send the curl_verbose.txt + app logs + any X-Request-ID values I'll open an internal trace with infra and runtime. Thanks all :thumbsup:
